name: First Contact
description: Discover the target's exposed services and find the lab's first contact marker.
hints: Scan the target and read full HTTP responses, not just bodies.
Some information lives in protocol metadata.
Look at HTTP response headers with curl -i.

name: Service Matrix
description: Not every service speaks HTTP on a well-known port. Map the full service matrix.
hints: The obvious ports are only part of the picture.
One hidden service answers on a high port in the 8xxx range.
Enumerate paths on the hidden service at :8081.

name: Shadow Services
description: The WAF gate hides a diagnostics page that describes the lab's shadow services.
hints: Find the service on port 5050 first.
Services often expose /health or /diag style paths.
Browse http://127.0.0.1:5050/diag/ports.

name: Banner Grabber
description: Grab service banners. One banner carries more than a version string.
hints: Connect to the plaintext file service on 2121.
Read the welcome banner before logging in.
Multi-line banners carry extra commentary.

name: HTTP Surface
description: Enumerate the web server's declared surface.
hints: Start with robots.txt.
robots.txt may reference a sitemap.
Fetch /sitemap.xml.

name: FTP-01 Anonymous Access
description: Log in to the FTP service without valid credentials.
hints: Some FTP servers allow a guest login.
Try user 'anonymous' with any email as password.
Default directory listing after anonymous login holds the flag.

name: FTP-02 Backup Discovery
description: A developer left a backup archive on the FTP server. Retrieve and inspect it.
hints: Look for archive files (.zip) after anonymous login.
Download backup.zip and extract it.
old_config.txt inside the archive is interesting.

name: FTP-03 Credential Reuse
description: A password found in an FTP backup works somewhere else. Prove the reuse.
hints: credentials.old inside the backup lists a service account.
That account is also an SSH user on port 2222.
Log into SSH as that user to collect the reuse flag.

name: FTP-04 Hidden Directory
description: A directory is deliberately excluded from listings. Find it anyway.
hints: LIST does not show dot-directories by default.
Try changing directory blind with CWD.
Try CWD .backup then LIST.

name: Telnet Enumeration
description: Identify the embedded management console and read its banner.
hints: Scan for the telnet-like service on a non-standard port.
Port 2323 is not the classic 23.
Read the full banner on connect.

name: Telnet Weak Credentials
description: Authenticate to the embedded management console using a leaked password.
hints: The password is not admin:admin.
An FTP file mentions an old employee's console password.
employee_notes.txt in the FTP home directory.

name: Telnet Config Disclosure
description: Once logged in, interrogate the console's configuration.
hints: The console supports a 'show' command.
Try: show config
Configuration leaks credentials used by other services.

name: Telnet Fuzzing
description: Fuzz the console inputs (username, password, terminal type, IAC negotiation) and capture the crash artifact.
hints: Send a username far longer than expected.
Telnet options (IAC) are structured input worth mutating.
Send 300+ bytes as username to trigger the length bug.

name: SSH Service Identification
description: Identify the SSH service on the non-standard port and obtain a session.
hints: SSH is not on port 22 here.
Find credentials from an earlier track.
Any valid login presents the lab MOTD with the flag.

name: SSH via SMB Credentials
description: Credentials found in an SMB share open an SSH session.
hints: Enumerate SMB shares first.
The backup share requires authentication.
Log into SSH as svc_backup.

name: SSH Key Authentication
description: A private key sits in an old backup. Use it to authenticate.
hints: backup.zip contains more than text files.
An id_rsa key is inside the archive.
Log in as user 'backup' with the key (password auth is disabled for that account).

name: SMB Enumeration
description: Enumerate shares, workgroup and OS hints on port 445.
hints: smbclient -L //target, or enum4linux.
nmap SMB scripts help too.
The public share's readme holds the flag.

name: SMB Anonymous Read
description: Read a share that allows guest access.
hints: Guest access works on one share.
Connect to \\target\public anonymously.
notes.txt in the public share.

name: SMB Old Backup Share
description: The backup share requires credentials. Find them and read old_backup.txt.
hints: Credentials leak from other tracks (FTP backup or telnet config).
svc_backup's password works here.
\\target\backup\old_backup.txt.

name: SMB Engineering Notes
description: Reach the engineering share and read its notes.
hints: Enumerate all share names, not just the obvious ones.
The telnet config leak names the engineering share credentials.
\\target\engineering\engineering_notes.txt.

name: SMB Hidden Share
description: One share is not advertised in the share list. Guess it.
hints: Hidden shares conventionally end with $.
Think like a developer: dev$, test$, tmp$.
Connect to \\target\dev$ directly.

name: robots.txt Discovery
description: Read the crawler rules and visit what they reveal.
hints: Fetch /robots.txt first on any site.
Disallowed paths are invitations.
/admin-old contains the flag; /not-the-flag does not.

name: HTML Comment
description: Developers leave comments in markup. Read the page source.
hints: View source, not rendered text.
Search the homepage HTML for comment markers.
grep for 'FLAG' in the response body.

name: Git Repository Leak
description: A .git directory was deployed to production. Recover history.
hints: Check /.git/HEAD.
Logs of refs reveal old commits.
Read /.git/logs/refs/heads/main for the removed password commit.

name: Config Backup File
description: Find the editor backup of the site configuration.
hints: File extensions like .bak, .old, ~ are classic backups.
Try /config.bak.
Backup configs leak keys and comments.

name: SQL Injection
description: The intranet search feature talks to SQLite. Make it return hidden rows.
hints: Search inputs that reach SQL are worth quoting.
Break out of the string: ' OR 1=1--
/search?q=' OR 1=1-- returns a row marked secret.

name: Debug Page Leak
description: A developer debug page was left enabled in production.
hints: There is a /debug route on the target.
It prints runtime diagnostics.
Read the diagnostic block for the flag.

name: Log Discovery
description: Application logs are web-accessible. Read them.
hints: Log files love predictable names under /logs/.
Try /logs/app.log.
Logs leak usernames, paths and developer mistakes.

name: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting
description: Prove the search page reflects unencoded input into the response.
hints: Reflect input like <script>alert(1)</script>.
The server rewards a successful reflection proof.
POST or GET the payload to /search and read the response.

name: API-01 Who Is Here?
description: The users endpoint returns far more than usernames.
hints: GET /api/v1/users
Response metadata is unusually chatty.
Read every field including meta/notes.

name: API-02 BOLA Profile Access
description: Object identifiers in /api/v1/profile/<id> are not authorization.
hints: Your profile is 1001.
Neighbouring identifiers belong to other people.
Fetch /api/v1/profile/1002.

name: API-03 Admin Enumeration
description: Look up the admin account and then read its profile.
hints: GET /api/v1/user?username=admin
Use the returned profile_id with /api/v1/profile/.
The admin profile's note field holds the flag.

name: API-04 Excessive Data Exposure
description: Hiding fields in the UI is not authorization. Request the raw object.
hints: The UI shows username and email only.
Raw API objects carry internal fields.
Read profile 1001's note field.

name: API-05 Client-Side Secret
description: An internal API key is shipped to browsers. Find it.
hints: Inspect static JavaScript, not just HTML.
/static/js/app.js
grep for VL_INTERNAL_KEY.

name: API-06 Admin Export
description: Use the leaked internal key on the admin export endpoint.
hints: GET /api/v1/admin/export
Send the key from app.js as X-Internal-Key.
Authorization by shared secret only.

name: API-07 Mass Assignment
description: The profile PATCH endpoint accepts properties the UI never sends.
hints: PATCH /api/v1/profile with JSON.
Send properties the form doesn't expose: role, is_admin.
Escalate to role=admin then re-read your profile.

name: API-08 Weak JWT Secret
description: Crack the JWT signing secret and mint an admin token.
hints: The token uses HS256.
Secrets leak in old configs and settings files.
config.bak / flask_settings.py both mention the lab secret.

name: API-09 Algorithm Confusion
description: The verifier has a fallback path for tokens with no signature.
hints: Inspect the JWT header: {"alg":...}.
Some libraries accept alg: none.
Forge a token with alg none and role admin.

name: API-10 Predictable Reset
description: Password reset tokens are derived, not random. Reset the admin account.
hints: POST /api/v1/reset with a username.
The token is a hash of predictable inputs.
md5(username + '1234') style derivation - see the research hint.

name: API-11 SSRF Fetch
description: The URL-preview endpoint fetches server-side. Make it fetch an internal resource.
hints: GET /api/v1/fetch?url=
Only lab-internal hosts are reachable - that's the point.
Fetch http://127.0.0.1:5000/internal/secret

name: API-12 Fake Metadata
description: An educational metadata endpoint imitates cloud instance metadata. Reach it through the fetch endpoint.
hints: Cloud metadata lives at 169.254.169.254 in the real world.
This lab serves a safe fake at /internal/metadata.
Fetch it via /api/v1/fetch.

name: API-13 Shadow API Inventory
description: Documented APIs are not all APIs. Inventory the undocumented versions.
hints: Version prefixes beyond /api/v1/ exist.
Try /api/v2/ and /api/internal/.
One undocumented route returns the flag.

name: API-14 OTP Rate Limit
description: The OTP endpoint barely limits attempts. Brute-force the 4-digit code.
hints: POST /api/v1/otp to request a code.
Send codes to /api/v1/otp/verify in a loop.
4 digits, no lockout: ~10000 requests.

name: API-15 CORS Misconfiguration
description: The CORS policy echoes any Origin back with credentials.
hints: Send an Origin header you control.
Observe Access-Control-Allow-Origin.
GET /api/v1/cors-demo with Origin: https://evil.test

name: API-16 Function-Level Authorization
description: A user-role token reaches an admin-only action.
hints: POST /api/v1/user/export with a normal user token.
Admin checks are missing on this route.
Any valid token works - that's the bug.

name: API-17 Fuzzing Lab
description: Fuzz /api/v1/fuzz with typed and malformed input and classify each response.
hints: Not every 4xx is a bug - read status semantics.
JSON type confusion (arrays/objects where scalars expected) is a category of its own.
Send x as an object to trigger the unhandled case.

name: GraphQL Schema Discovery
description: Introspect the GraphQL endpoint and dump the schema.
hints: POST /graphql with a query.
Introspection query: {__schema{types{name,fields{name}}}}
Hidden types/fields appear in the dump.

name: GraphQL Authorization Bypass
description: The server blocks the sensitive field name but not its aliases.
hints: Querying internalSecret directly is blocked.
GraphQL supports aliases: alias: field.
Use { leaked: internalSecret }.

name: GraphQL Query Complexity
description: Query depth/complexity limits are enforced superficially. Abuse batching.
hints: Depth limits don't stop aliases or batches.
Send an array of queries in one request.
Batch more than 8 queries to hit the debug path.

name: WAF 403 Bypass
description: /admin on port 5050 always answers 403. The deny rule is exact-match. Find the route anyway.
hints: The filter compares the raw path for exact equality.
Routing normalizes the path before matching.
Try a trailing slash: /admin/

name: Header Trust
description: An internal panel trusts a proxy-supplied client identity header.
hints: Reverse proxies commonly set X-Forwarded-For.
The app trusts it without validation.
Request /internal-panel with X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1

name: HTTP Method Authorization
description: GET /admin/action is blocked. Authorization must not depend on method.
hints: Only one method is checked.
Try POST, PUT, PATCH on the same path.
POST /admin/action is authorized.

name: 406 Filter Mismatch
description: The filter scans the raw body; the backend decodes it. Prove the parser mismatch.
hints: 406 means the filter didn't like your input.
The keyword filter sees raw bytes only.
Send the keyword as \uXXXX escapes in a JSON body.

name: Double-Decode Traversal
description: The filter blocks '..' after one decode; the backend decodes twice.
hints: /download?file= is filtered for '..'.
URL-encode a percent sign to get double encoding.
Use %252e%252e%252f to reach /secret/flag.txt

name: Upload Extension Filter
description: The extension denylist is case-sensitive.
hints: .php is blocked.
Filters compare byte-for-byte.
Upload flag.pHp (mixed case).

name: Upload Content-Type Trust
description: The server trusts the client-supplied Content-Type.
hints: Set Content-Type: image/png on a non-image body.
Multipart metadata is attacker-controlled.
Upload with a spoofed content type.

name: Upload Path Traversal
description: The filename is joined to the upload directory without sanitization.
hints: Filename is attacker controlled.
Include ../ in the filename.
Write outside uploads/ and observe the response.

name: Stored HTML/SVG Upload
description: Uploaded HTML/SVG is served inline with its original content type.
hints: .html and .svg are allowed types.
The server serves uploads back with their content type.
Upload an .svg then fetch /files/<name> and read the response header.

name: Crypto ECB Identification
description: Identify the block cipher mode used by the token oracle.
hints: Identical plaintext blocks produce identical ciphertext blocks.
That pattern is the definition of one mode.
Submit the mode name at /crypto/ecb?mode=ECB

name: Crypto Predictable RNG
description: Session tokens come from a seeded PRNG. Predict the next one.
hints: seed = current time in seconds.
Reproduce the generator locally.
Claim the predicted token at /crypto/token/claim.

name: Crypto CBC Bit Flipping
description: CBC ciphertext with no MAC is malleable. Flip role=user to role=admin.
hints: IV is published alongside the ciphertext.
Flipping a ciphertext block alters the next plaintext block.
Verify the modified blob at /crypto/verify.

name: Crypto Hash Length Extension
description: The API signs messages as sha256(secret || message). Forge a signature without the secret.
hints: Secret-prefix MACs are length-extension friendly.
Append your payload and compute the continuation state.
Forge a signature for msg ending in &role=admin.

name: CVE Hunter: FTP fingerprint
description: Product: vsftpd / Version: 2.3.4. Which historical CVE is associated with this version? (research only)
hints: This version is famous for a backdoored release.
Search NVD for vsftpd 2.3.4 backdoor.

name: CVE Hunter: ProFTPD mod_copy
description: Product: ProFTPD / Component: mod_copy / Issue: arbitrary file copy leading to RCE. Identify the CVE.
hints: mod_copy SITE CPFR/CPTO misuse.
Search NVD for ProFTPD mod_copy 2019.

name: CVE Hunter: SMBv1 EternalBlue
description: Protocol: SMBv1 / Windows SMB server. Identify the remote code execution CVE from 2017.
hints: WannaCry-era vulnerability.
Patch: MS17-010.

name: CVE Hunter: SMBv3.1.1 Compression
description: Protocol: SMBv3.1.1 / Feature: compression handling. Identify the 2020 critical RCE CVE.
hints: Pre-auth RCE in the compression driver.
Codename: SMBGhost.

name: CVE Hunter: OpenSSH regreSSHion
description: Service: sshd / Issue: signal-handling race (CVE-2006-era regression, disclosed 2024). Identify the CVE.
hints: A regression of a 2006 bug.
Public name: regreSSHion.

name: CVE Hunter: Telnetd stack overflow
description: Product: NETGEAR RAX30 telnetd / Issue: stack-based buffer overflow with root RCE. Identify the CVE.
hints: Consumer router telnet service.
2023 disclosure affecting RAX30.

name: CVE Hunter: IPCOMShell TELNET
description: Product: Interpeak IPCOMShell TELNET server / Issue: heap overflow with memory corruption. Identify the CVE.
hints: Embedded shell product from the mid-2010s.
Search NVD for IPCOMShell.

name: CVE Hunter: Tenda Telnet injection
description: Product: Tenda AC9 firmware / Issue: command injection via Telnet functionality. Identify the CVE.
hints: 2025-dated advisory.
Consumer router OS command injection.

name: CWE Hunter: Untrusted Deserialization
description: Scenario: an application deserializes attacker-influenced objects from a cache. Which CWE applies? (format: CWE-NNN)
hints: It is a weakness classification, not a CVE.
Language-agnostic: unsafe object reconstruction.
CWE-502

name: CWE Hunter: Spoofed Proxy Identity
description: Scenario: an application authenticates clients by a spoofable X-Forwarded-For header. Which CWE? (format: CWE-NNN)
hints: Authentication by attacker-controlled identity.
CWE-290 area: authentication bypass by spoofing.
CWE-290

name: FLASK-01 Template Injection Detection
description: Is /profile?name= evaluated by the template engine? Prove it with a harmless expression.
hints: Send {{7*7}} as the name parameter.
If 49 comes back, the input is a template.
/profile?name={{7*7}}

name: FLASK-02 Jinja Runtime Escape
description: Use template injection to read the lab flag file for this challenge.
hints: Find the configured flag directory (/internal/config).
Escape into the Python object graph from the template context.
Read <flagdir>/ssti.flag through the Jinja runtime.

name: FLASK-03 SSTI Filter Failure
description: /safe-profile blocks suspicious words. Prove a blacklist is not a sandbox.
hints: Blocked: import, eval, os, subprocess, flag (words, not behavior).
Construct attribute access dynamically with |attr.
Fetch the path via request.args so the word 'flag' never appears.

name: FLASK-04 Debug Mode Exposed
description: A development instance with debugging enabled is running on the lab network.
hints: A hidden service listens on port 8000.
Its / page carries a traceback-style footer.
Find the comment marked FLASK-04.

name: FLASK-05 Debugger PIN Investigation
description: The debugger console is protected by a PIN derived from predictable machine attributes. Compute the lab PIN and submit it.
hints: Research how debugger PINs are generated (public research).
/debug-lab/info lists username, app path, mac and machine id.
Combine those attributes with the documented md5 grouping into a 6-3 PIN.

name: FLASK-06 Debug Console
description: Use the debugger console to read the lab flag file.
hints: Enter the computed PIN at /debug-lab/console.
Evaluate an expression that opens a file.
Read <flagdir>/debugger.flag.

name: FLASK-07 Weak Application Secret
description: The Flask session signing key is a weak, leaked string. Find it.
hints: Leaked source/settings files are prime suspects.
static/leaks/flask_settings.py
Any string used to sign cookies can be cracked.

name: FLASK-08 Session Integrity
description: Forge an administrator session cookie and visit /admin.
hints: Flask cookies are itsdangerous-signed payloads.
Use the leaked secret with flask.session.dumps or itsdangerous.
Set role=admin then GET /admin.

name: FLASK-09 Cache Identification
description: Identify which caching component and serialization format the app uses.
hints: GET /api/v1/cache/info
Read the serializer field.
The response also carries the flag.

name: FLASK-10 Pickle Discovery
description: Find the cache backend source leak and identify the serializer.
hints: Developer source files leak under /static/leaks/.
cache_backend.py documents the storage format.
Read the FLASK-10 comment.

name: FLASK-11 Cache Architecture
description: Map where cache objects physically live.
hints: GET /api/v1/cache/stats
Cache files sit on local disk under ./data/cache.
The stats response carries the flag.

name: FLASK-12 Unsafe Deserialization
description: Write an attacker-controlled pickle into the cache store and have the app deserialize it.
hints: Upload path traversal can write outside uploads/.
Place a pickle at data/cache/<key>.pkl.
Then GET /api/v1/cache/get?key=<key>.

name: FLASK-13 CVE-2021-33026
description: Component: Flask-Caching (through 1.10.1) / Issue: unsafe pickle serialization in cache backends. Which CVE?
hints: Research the Flask-Caching pickle issue and its prerequisites.
Prerequisites matter: cache poisoning or attacker control of the backend.

name: FLASK-14 Controlled RCE
description: Use the deserialization path to execute a lab command and read the RCE flag file.
hints: Your pickle payload can run OS commands.
Read <flagdir>/rce.flag.
The response also reveals a service credential - chain it into SSH.

name: FLASK-BOSS Three Doors
description: There are three ways into this application's Python runtime: template injection, the debugger, and deserialization. Understand them and solve two.
hints: SSTI, Werkzeug debugger, pickle cache.
Two of flask-02 / flask-06 / flask-12 must be solved first.
The flag unlocks once two doors are open.

name: Local Enumeration
description: You have a user shell. Enumerate the machine before exploiting anything.
hints: id, uname, sudo -l, find, crontab, env.
Look in /opt/vulnlab.
Read /opt/vulnlab/README.local.

name: SUID Discovery
description: Find SUID binaries and the lab's suid notes.
hints: find / -perm -4000 2>/dev/null
Notes live under /usr/local/share/vulnlab.
Read suid.flag there.

name: SUID Exploitation
description: /usr/local/bin/vulnhelper runs as root and takes a file argument. Make it read a root-owned flag.
hints: ls -l shows the SUID bit.
--read takes any path (no validation).
Run: vulnhelper --read /root/suid.flag

name: Writable Cron Script
description: A root cron job runs a script the lab user can write.
hints: sudo -l and /etc/cron.d/vulnlab both matter.
/opt/vulnlab/maintenance.sh is writable and runs as root.
Overwrite it, then run it with sudo.

name: PATH Hijack
description: A root scheduled task calls a command without an absolute path.
hints: Read /etc/cron.d/vulnlab carefully - no leading slash on one command.
/opt/vulnlab/bin is writable and on the job's PATH.
Plant log-cleaner there, then trigger lab-tick.

name: Environment Secret
description: A leaked environment variable unlocks an encrypted local file.
hints: env and /proc/self/environ show inherited variables.
VULNLAB_BACKUP_KEY is exported.
vulnlab-decrypt /var/backups/creds.enc

name: Configuration Secrets
description: Service configuration files hold more than settings.
hints: /etc/vulnlab/
Read app.conf.
Configuration files reward careless comments.

name: Cron Discovery
description: Inventory scheduled tasks on the machine.
hints: Look in /etc/cron.d/.
cat /etc/cron.d/vulnlab
A comment in the job file holds the flag.

name: Business Logic: Negative Quantity
description: The shop never validates quantity sign. Order with a negative amount.
hints: POST /api/v1/shop/order
Send qty=-1.
Your balance increases instead of decreasing.

name: Business Logic: Race Condition
description: Balance check and deduction are separate steps. Redeem the same coupon twice concurrently.
hints: POST /api/v1/redeem with the coupon field.
Fire several requests at the same time.
Two successful redeems yield the flag.

name: Business Logic: Client Price
description: The client controls the price it pays. Buy the ROOT_ACCESS_TOKEN cheap.
hints: POST /api/v1/shop/order accepts a price field.
Override price to 1 for the 100000-credit item.
Buy ROOT_ACCESS_TOKEN for 1 credit.

name: Hidden Backup File
description: Dotfiles are invisible until you look for them.
hints: In the user shell: ls -a everywhere.
/var/backups is a classic location.
cat /var/backups/.hidden

name: JavaScript Source Map
description: minified JavaScript often ships its source map.
hints: app.js ends with a sourceMappingURL comment.
Fetch /static/js/app.js.map.
The map contains developer-embedded comments.

name: Old Employee Notes
description: An FTP file documents an account nobody disabled.
hints: FTP anonymous home directory.
employee_notes.txt
The note itself carries the flag.

name: Process Environment
description: Inspect the process environment in the user shell.
hints: /proc/self/environ is NUL-delimited - use tr or grep.
Look for VULNLAB_BONUS_ENV.
cat /proc/self/environ | tr '\0' '\n'

name: Dead Debug Endpoint
description: A decommissioned debug route still answers with a marker.
hints: robots.txt lists /debug-old.
Compare it with /debug.
Read the X-Lab-Flag header of /debug-old.

name: Private Area
description: robots.txt disallows /private. Follow it.
hints: robots.txt again.
/private is reachable despite robots.
Read the page.

name: Log Poisoning Artifact
description: Something was logged that shouldn't have been.
hints: /logs/app.log contains several interesting lines.
Search for VULNLAB{ in the log.
One line records an internal debug call.

name: Stale Cache Entry
description: A pre-warmed cache entry contains leftover data.
hints: GET /api/v1/cache/get?key=demo
Cached objects keep their old payloads.
Read the returned object.

name: Flask Chain Completion
description: A credential revealed by a Flask attack path opens SSH. Complete the chain.
hints: One of the Flask RCE routes exposes svc_flask's password.
Log into SSH on 2222 as svc_flask.
The login banner carries the chain flag.

name: ROOT OF VULNLAB
description: You have compromised multiple components of the machine. Obtain root and capture the final flag. Requires linux-01.
hints: Enumerate before exploiting: SUID, sudo, cron, PATH.
There is more than one way to root.
cat /root/root.txt as root.

name: CSRF-01 Forged Role Change
description: Change a user's role without a CSRF token.
hints: The endpoint only checks the session cookie.
Any page can auto-submit the form for a logged-in admin.
solution: POST /admin/users/role with a forged admin session cookie.
solution: The response confirms what it changed.

name: CSRF-02 Optional Origin Check
description: Bypass an origin check that only runs when the header is present.
hints: The comparison is inside an `if origin or referer`.
An attacker controls whether the browser sends those headers.
solution: POST /admin/settings with neither Origin nor Referer.
solution: The response says whether the check actually ran.

name: HOST-01 Reset Link Poisoning
description: Poison the password-reset link with the Host header.
hints: The link is built from whatever host the client claims.
X-Forwarded-Host is preferred over Host.
solution: GET /auth/reset-link?user=student with a Host you control.
solution: `poisoned: true` means the link now points at you.

name: HOST-02 Forwarded Host Wins
description: Make the application generate an absolute URL for an attacker domain.
hints: X-Forwarded-Host overrides the real host.
There is no proxy here that would overwrite it.
solution: GET /portal/absolute-url with X-Forwarded-Host set.
solution: `trusted: false` is the confirmation.

name: RESP-01 Response Splitting
description: Smuggle a second header through a redirect parameter.
hints: `next` is copied into a header without validation.
Try the CRLF variant of the parameter.
solution: GET /go?raw= with an encoded CRLF sequence.
solution: `injected: true` confirms the split.

name: REDIR-01 Protocol-Relative Open Redirect
description: Redirect off-site through a path that looks local.
hints: The check only looks for a leading single slash.
`//host` is a protocol-relative URL.
solution: GET /portal/continue?next=//evil.test/
solution: `external: true` confirms it left the site.

name: SQLI-01 Blind Injection via Row Count
description: Extract data from a lookup that never reflects its results.
hints: The body is blind, but a debug header leaks the row count.
A username lookup should match exactly one row.
solution: GET /api/v1/lookup?user= with a UNION or OR payload.
solution: Watch the X-Rows response header.

name: SQLI-02 Second-Order Injection
description: Store a payload now, trigger it when an admin views a report.
hints: Nothing fires when you save it.
The stored value goes back into a query later.

name: CMDI-01 Command Injection in Diagnostics
description: Break out of a shell command through the ping target.
hints: The host parameter is concatenated into a shell string.
Command substitution is enough.
solution: GET /tools/ping?host= with a substitution or `;` payload.
solution: The output shows the result of your extra command.

name: XXE-01 External Entity File Read
description: Read a local file through an XML external entity.
hints: The import endpoint parses XML with entities enabled.
Point the entity at a lab file.
solution: POST /api/v1/import with a DOCTYPE and SYSTEM entity.
solution: `read_local_file: true` confirms the read.

name: RACE-01 Replayable Single-Use Token
description: Redeem a one-time token more than once.
hints: The value is granted before the token is invalidated.
You do not need to win a timing race.
solution: POST /portal/redeem with the same nonce twice.
solution: The second response reports the replay.

name: ADMIN-01 Spoofed Client Address
description: Open an admin console that trusts a header for identity.
hints: The allow-list checks X-Forwarded-For, not the socket.
No proxy sits in front to strip it.
solution: GET /admin/console with X-Forwarded-For: 10.0.0.5.
solution: `console: opened` confirms the bypass.

name: XSS-02 DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting
description: Execute script through a client-side sink that the server never sees.
hints: /portal/announcement puts the URL fragment into innerHTML.
The server cannot observe JavaScript, so the page beacons it.
solution: Load /portal/announcement#<script>...</script> with x=dom in the fragment.
solution: The beacon at /api/v1/xss/beacon is only reached if the sink ran.

name: XSS-03 Attribute-Context Breakout

hints: The bio is escaped - but for a text context, not an attribute one.
You need to escape the quote character too.
solution: POST /api/v1/profile/bio with a payload containing a double quote.
